title: Story Paths
description: Read short passages and understand their meaning

passages.text: Maya found a small bird in her garden. Its wing was hurt. She carefully picked it up and brought it inside. Her grandmother helped her make a soft bed for the bird.
passages.question: What did Maya find?

passages.text: The rain fell softly on the roof. Inside, the family gathered around the table. Grandpa told stories about when he was young. Everyone listened quietly.
passages.question: What was Grandpa doing?

passages.text: Kofi loved to draw. Every day after school, he would sit by the window and draw what he saw. Today he drew the big tree outside. The leaves were changing colors.
passages.question: When did Kofi draw?

passages.text: The market was busy and colorful. People sold fruits, vegetables, and cloth. Amara helped her mother carry the basket. They bought mangoes and tomatoes.
passages.question: Where were Amara and her mother?

passages.text: Jamal's baby sister was crying. He remembered that she liked the sound of his voice. So he sat next to her and sang a gentle song. Soon, she stopped crying and smiled.
passages.question: Why did Jamal sing to his sister?
options: Because their mom asked him to

passages.text: The garden had been dry for weeks. Nadia's grandmother looked worried. Then one morning, dark clouds appeared. By afternoon, rain was falling. Grandmother smiled and said, 'The plants will be happy now.'
passages.question: Why was grandmother worried at first?
options: The plants were growing too fast

passages.text: Esi practiced her speech many times. She stood in front of the mirror and spoke clearly. She wanted to do well at the school assembly. When the day came, she felt ready.
passages.question: Why did Esi practice so much?
options: She had nothing else to do

levels.name: Making Connections
levels.description: Think about what happens next or what it means

passages.text: Every Saturday, the elders gathered under the old baobab tree. They shared stories of the past and gave advice to the young people. Marcus always sat close and listened carefully. He knew these stories were precious gifts.
passages.question: What can we understand about Marcus?
options: He already knows all the stories

passages.text: Fatima noticed that her neighbor, Mr. Johnson, hadn't picked up his newspaper in three days. She told her mother. Together, they went to check on him. Mr. Johnson had been sick and was grateful for their help.
passages.question: What does this story teach us?

passages.text: The river had been part of the community for generations. People fished there, children played by its banks, and families gathered for celebrations. When some people wanted to build a factory nearby, the community came together to protect their river.
passages.question: Why did the community want to protect the river?
options: It was important to their way of life
passages.answer: It was important to their way of life

levels.name: Deeper Meaning
levels.description: Think about bigger ideas in stories

passages.text: The young drummer watched his grandfather's hands move across the djembe. Each rhythm told a story. His grandfather said, 'When I am gone, these rhythms will still be here—in your hands.' The boy understood that some things are passed down like treasures.
passages.question: What was the grandfather teaching his grandson?
options: That traditions carry forward through generations
passages.answer: That traditions carry forward through generations

passages.text: Two neighbors argued over where the property line was. For weeks, they didn't speak. Then one day, a storm knocked down trees on both their yards. Working together to clear the debris, they began talking again. By evening, the property line seemed less important.
passages.question: What did the neighbors learn?
options: Working together matters more than small disagreements
passages.answer: Working together matters more than small disagreements

passages.text: An old woman walked slowly through the village each morning. Some young people laughed at how slowly she moved. But the village elder told them, 'She has walked more miles than you can imagine. Every step she takes now carries the weight of a lifetime of journeys.'
passages.question: What is the elder teaching the young people?
options: To respect the experiences of elders
passages.answer: To respect the experiences of elders

passages.text: The library had been closed for months. When it finally reopened, people of all ages came. A young girl asked the librarian why so many people were there. The librarian smiled and said, 'Books hold the thoughts of people we'll never meet and places we'll never go. People missed having access to all those worlds.'
passages.question: According to the librarian, why are books valuable?
options: They connect us to ideas beyond our own experience
passages.answer: They connect us to ideas beyond our own experience
